Triage: graded to `needs-user-decision` + routed `domain:cli` (the gate lives in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` — runtime is cli-lane; whatever supplies FLS comes later, from wherever the ruling points). The card's own instinct is right: this is a domain-level read-authorization *policy* that has never been stated, it is a security/permission boundary (human floor — not auto-adjudicable), and PR #7896 turning the snapshot unconditional supplies the pull that #4829 says is the moment to ask.

Four-lens block (①–④ per #7498):

- **① Platform long-term coherence** — the platform currently answers the same question two ways depending on the door: `/automation` run-detail = "authenticated is enough", `sys_automation_run.variables_json` = system-object permissions. One stated policy collapses the incoherence; leaving it unstated grows it with every new automation read route.
- **② Measured business pull** — measured, not speculative: any authenticated caller with a run id reads the triggering record's fields with no FLS applied, and since PR #7896 that data is in every paused run rather than only author-opted-in outputs. No customer report yet; exposure class is real.
- **③ AI-agent error-resistance** — "per-field filtering of a free-form variable map" is not mechanically decidable (only some keys correspond to record fields at all); a policy an agent can implement wrongly-but-quietly is worse than a coarse one it cannot. The decidable options are coarse: gate the read on a permission, or don't.
- **④ Startup scope discipline** — the cheapest coherent option is convergence, not invention: gate `/automation` run-detail (and kin) on the same permission the `sys_automation_run` object read already answers with, so two doors give one answer and no new FLS machinery is built.

**Recommendation: converge the doors** — require the caller to pass the `sys_automation_run` object-read permission for run-detail (and audit the other `/automation` reads against the same rule), explicitly rejecting per-field filtering of the variables map as ill-defined. Narrowing cost (existing operator tooling must hold that permission) is the price of having a policy at all; if the maintainer prefers "authenticated is enough" as the deliberate policy, writing THAT down also closes this card.

Not dispatchable until ruled; exits the finding stock into the decision box (label kept as `finding`+`needs-user-decision` deliberately: it is both a graded observation and an open ruling, the #7732 combo shape).

## Maintainer ruling — 2026-08-12

**Ruled: converge the two doors — the `/automation` read surface requires the same permission the `sys_automation_run` object read answers with; per-field filtering of the variables map is rejected as the mechanism.**

Provenance: maintainer, triage PM session chat (`session_01NKGoRBFZELVKivDkiAswdz`), 2026-08-12, verbatim: 「7918 A,7917 ②,7900 收敛两扇门,7929 来源标记」. Recorded by the triage seat; `needs-user-decision`/`finding` → `pm:queue` swapped in the same write.

Implementation boundaries:
- Landing: `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` — run-detail first (the measured exposure), then audit every other `/automation` read route against the same rule; routes that stay authenticated-only after the audit need a stated reason in the PR, not silence.
- The permission consulted is the `sys_automation_run` object-read grant (however plugin-security exposes that check to the runtime domain) — one policy, two doors, one answer.
- ⛔ Do not build per-field filtering of `variables` — explicitly rejected by this ruling (mechanically undecidable per the card's measurement).
- Migration note the PR must state: operator tooling that previously read run detail with bare authentication now needs the grant — call it out in the changeset so deployments can pre-grant.
- Refusal tests assert `code` + `status`; positive control: a caller WITH the grant reads exactly what they read today.
- Fork clause: if implementation shows the object-permission check cannot be reached from the runtime domain without a new cross-package seam, report the shape before building it — don't invent a second permission system silently.

**Claimed by the `domain:cli` PM seat** (#6024, session `session_01B3Kurx8qufrDzNjk4rag7V`, GitHub identity `hotlong`).
Branch: `claude/issue-7900-automation-read-permission-gate` · dispatch: `mode:cloud`, `model: claude-opus-5`.

Dispatching on the **maintainer ruling above** — that comment is the spec, and this seat adds nothing to it. Two things I am pinning rather than leaving to the executor:

**The audit half is not optional.** The ruling says run-detail first, *then* audit every other `/automation` read route against the same rule, and that a route staying authenticated-only needs a **stated reason in the PR, not silence**. A PR that fixes run-detail and says nothing about the rest is incomplete even if run-detail is perfect — the whole point of the ruling is that the domain gets one policy. The PR body carries a route-by-route table.

**The fork clause is a stop, not a hint.** If the `sys_automation_run` object-read check cannot be reached from the runtime domain without a new cross-package seam, **report the shape and stop**. Inventing a second permission system quietly is the failure mode the ruling names, and it would be worse than this card staying open another day. Coming back with "here is the seam that would be required" is a success outcome.

Restating the ⛔ so it cannot be softened in implementation: **do not build per-field filtering of the `variables` map.** The ruling rejects it as the mechanism, on the card's own measurement that it is mechanically undecidable — only some keys correspond to a record field at all.

Standard lane pins on top: refusal asserts `code` **and** `status` (ADR-0112); the positive control is that a caller **with** the grant reads exactly what they read today (this is the pin that proves a narrowing rather than a breakage); reverse-verify the refusal test against the un-gated code and report the observed output.

Migration text belongs in the **changeset**, per the ruling — operator tooling that read run detail with bare authentication now needs the grant, and deployments need to be able to pre-grant before upgrading.
